0.0.n: Combined with 月, this number names April.

0.1.n: After a number, 月 names a calendar month; 4月 is April.

0.2.n: Marks April as the time when the outing happened.

0.3.n: A casual filler that keeps the listener engaged.

0.5.n: With で, this describes everyone doing something together.

0.6.n: Marks the group taking part in the outing.

0.7.n: Repeats the casual filler, giving the story a relaxed, conversational rhythm.

0.9.n: Although it can mean cooked rice, here it refers to eating a meal.

0.10.n: 食べ is the shortened verb form used before に to express the purpose of going.

0.11.n: After 食べ, に marks eating as the purpose of going.

0.12.n: The plain past form of 行く describes the outing before 時.

0.13.n: Follows the description of the outing to refer to that occasion.

0.14.n: Links that occasion to the photo taken then.

0.15.n: This is what turned up; the subject-marking particle が is omitted in casual speech.

0.16.n: 出て + きた describes something coming into view, here a photo being rediscovered.

1.0.n: Expresses warm feelings about something remembered from the past.

1.1.n: Invites the listener to share the speaker’s nostalgic feeling.

2.0.n: Repeating the adjective agrees with the other speaker’s nostalgic reaction.

3.0.n: An interjection expressing surprise at something the speaker has noticed.

3.2.n: Makes the observation sound tentative rather than definite.

3.3.n: Refers to how the person dressed previously.

3.4.n: Marks the earlier appearance as the point of comparison.

3.5.n: Refers to the clothes the listener wears.

3.6.n: Connects 服 to 系統, specifying that the style concerns clothing.

3.7.n: Here it refers to the general category or look of someone’s clothing.

3.8.n: Plain past form of 変わる; rising intonation makes it a casual question.

4.0.n: Casual shortened form of やっぱり, presenting a preference the speaker comes back to.

4.1.n: Slang for relaxed, low-effort clothing worn for comfort.

4.2.n: Identifies loungewear as the thing being described as comfortable.

4.3.n: Describes clothing that feels easy to wear without fuss.

4.4.n: The plain, casual form used to finish the statement after 楽.

4.5.n: Adds friendly emphasis to the speaker’s opinion.

0.lit: In April, you know, everyone together, you know, a photo from when we went to eat turned up.
0.tip: A verb’s shortened form + に行く means going to do something: 食べに行く is going out to eat.

1.tip: 懐かしい expresses fond memories, and ね invites the other person to share that feeling.

2.tip: Repeating the same adjective is a natural way to agree without explicitly saying yes.

3.lit: Huh, somehow, compared with before, has your style of clothes changed?
3.tip: 前と sets up a comparison with before; the question asks whether the clothing style has changed.

4.lit: After all, loungewear is comfortable, I tell you.
4.tip: ダル着 is slang for comfy, low-effort clothing, not a formal fashion category.
